quests.instruction: Which flat tool with numbers helps you draw a straight line?
quests.hint: The numbers along its edge are measurements.
quests.explanation: A ruler keeps your line straight and also tells you how long things are.
quests.funFact: Many rulers show centimeters on one edge and inches on the other.

quests.instruction: Which one shows the days and months of the year?
quests.hint: You can flip to a new page when a month ends.
quests.explanation: A calendar helps us plan ahead, like when a test, a holiday, or a birthday is coming.
quests.funFact: A normal year has 365 days, and a leap year has 366.

quests.instruction: Which round model shows the countries and oceans of the Earth?
quests.hint: You can spin it to see different parts of the world.
quests.explanation: A globe is a small model of the Earth, so you can see where countries and oceans are.
quests.funFact: About 70 percent of the Earth's surface is covered by water.

quests.instruction: Which instrument do you hit with sticks or your hands to make a beat?
quests.hint: You don't press keys or pluck strings for this one.
quests.explanation: A drum makes sound when its stretched top vibrates after you hit it.
quests.funFact: Drums are one of the oldest instruments, and people have played them for thousands of years.

quests.instruction: Which item do you kick or throw in sports games on the field?
quests.hint: It is round and bounces or rolls.
quests.explanation: Different sports use different balls, but they are all used to play together as a team.
quests.funFact: Cricket balls, footballs, and basketballs are different sizes because each sport has its own rules.

quests.instruction: Which big room is for exercise and games, even when the weather is bad?
quests.hint: Basketball hoops and floor lines are a clue.
quests.explanation: The gym gives students space to run and play indoors, so PE can go on when it rains.
quests.funFact: 'Gym' comes from an ancient Greek word that meant a place for exercise.

quests.instruction: Who helps you find the right book in the library?
quests.hint: This person works among the book shelves all day.
quests.explanation: A librarian looks after the books and helps students find stories and facts they like.
quests.funFact: Librarians arrange books so each one has its own place on the shelf.

quests.instruction: Who do you visit at school if you feel sick or get hurt?
quests.hint: Think of the person with a first aid box.
quests.explanation: The school nurse looks after students who feel unwell or have a small injury.
quests.funFact: School nurses also help keep a record of students' health needs, like allergies.

quests.instruction: Who serves the lunch and keeps the cafeteria running?
quests.hint: They work behind the lunch counter.
quests.explanation: Cafeteria workers prepare and serve meals so students have food to learn and play.
quests.funFact: Cafeteria teams often begin preparing meals hours before lunchtime.

quests.instruction: Which small box carries a meal that you bring from home?
quests.hint: It's the right size for a meal, not for books.
quests.explanation: A lunchbox keeps your food clean and together until it's time to eat.
quests.funFact: In India, many students carry their lunch in a tiffin box.

quests.instruction: Which soft paper helps you wipe sticky fingers after you eat?
quests.hint: It's for cleaning your hands, not for writing.
quests.explanation: A napkin wipes food off your hands and mouth so you stay tidy.
quests.funFact: Washing your hands before eating helps keep germs away from your food.

quests.instruction: What do you refill at school so you can sip water through the day?
quests.hint: It has a lid, and you can carry it with you.
quests.explanation: A water bottle lets you drink whenever you are thirsty, instead of waiting for lunchtime.
quests.funFact: Water makes up more than half of your body.

quests.instruction: Which small zipped bag keeps your pencils and erasers together?
quests.hint: Small tools go in, and the zip keeps them from falling out.
quests.explanation: A pencil case keeps small things in one place, so you can find them quickly.
quests.funFact: The modern zipper was developed in the early 1900s.

quests.instruction: Where does used paper go so it can be turned into new paper?
quests.hint: This bin is marked with a special green symbol.
quests.explanation: Paper in the recycling bin can be made into new paper instead of being thrown away.
quests.funFact: Paper can be recycled several times before its fibers get too short to use again.

quests.instruction: Where do books stand in rows in the classroom?
quests.hint: It's tall, with flat shelves for books to rest on.
quests.explanation: A bookshelf keeps books in an easy-to-find place, so everyone can borrow them.
quests.funFact: The Dewey Decimal system, created in 1876, groups library books by number.

quests.instruction: Which machine has a screen and keyboard and helps you type and look things up?
quests.hint: Its keys let you type letters and numbers.
quests.explanation: Computers help students type, search for facts, and make projects.
quests.funFact: The first computer mouse was made of wood.

quests.instruction: What do you wear over your ears to listen without disturbing others?
quests.hint: You can hear the sound, but the people nearby cannot.
quests.explanation: Headphones let you listen to lessons or music quietly. Keep the volume low to protect your ears.
quests.funFact: Listening to loud sounds for a long time can hurt your hearing.

quests.instruction: Which machine shines a big picture onto a wall or screen for the whole class?
quests.hint: A beam of light comes out of the front.
quests.explanation: A projector makes a small image big, so a whole class can see it together.
quests.funFact: A projector shines light through a lens to make the image larger.

quests.instruction: Which tool makes tiny things look bigger?
quests.hint: You hold it up close to the thing you want to look at.
quests.explanation: A magnifying glass has a curved lens that bends light so small things appear larger.
quests.funFact: Eyeglasses with magnifying lenses appeared in Italy about 700 years ago.

quests.instruction: Which living thing can a class water and watch grow?
quests.hint: It needs water, light, and air to live.
quests.explanation: Students can see how a plant grows when it gets water and light.
quests.funFact: Plants make their own food using sunlight, water, and air.

quests.instruction: Which tool tells you how hot or cold something is?
quests.hint: It has a scale of numbers for temperature.
quests.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature, so we know whether something is hot, warm, or cold.
quests.funFact: Water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius and boils at 100 degrees Celsius.

quests.instruction: Which frame with sliding beads helps you count?
quests.hint: You slide the beads along rods to count.
quests.explanation: An abacus lets you count by sliding beads, so you can see numbers as groups.
quests.funFact: People have used abaci for counting for thousands of years.

quests.instruction: Which paper shows where roads, towns, and rivers are?
quests.hint: It is a picture of a place seen from above.
quests.explanation: A map shows where places are, so people can find their way.
quests.funFact: Many maps have a key that explains what the colors and symbols mean.

quests.instruction: Which poster shows all the letters in order?
quests.hint: Look for the one with A at the beginning.
quests.explanation: An alphabet chart helps you remember the order and shape of letters.
quests.funFact: The English alphabet has 26 letters.

quests.instruction: Where would you go to hand in a note or ask the school staff a question?
quests.hint: Phones ring and staff answer questions here.
quests.explanation: The school office handles messages, notes, and questions for students and families.
quests.funFact: Visitors to a school usually check in at the office first.

quests.instruction: In which room do students sing and play instruments?
quests.hint: Look for drums and keyboards.
quests.explanation: In the music room, students learn to sing, keep a beat, and play instruments together.
quests.funFact: Instruments are grouped into families like strings, wind, and percussion.

quests.instruction: Which room has rows of computers for lessons?
quests.hint: Screens and keyboards are lined up on the tables.
quests.explanation: The computer lab gives each student a computer for typing, research, and projects.
quests.funFact: Early computers were so large that they filled a whole room.

quests.instruction: Which clothes do many students wear so everyone at the school looks alike?
quests.hint: The school chooses the colors and the style.
quests.explanation: A uniform shows that students belong to the same school.
quests.funFact: School uniforms are worn in many countries, including India, Japan, and the UK.

quests.instruction: Which do you wear on your feet to run safely during PE?
quests.hint: Look for shoes that stay on firmly and have a grip.
quests.explanation: Sports shoes protect your feet and grip the floor, so you don't slip when you run.
quests.funFact: Sports shoes have soft soles that cushion each step.

quests.instruction: What keeps you dry on the walk to school when it rains?
quests.hint: Open it up above your head.
quests.explanation: An umbrella keeps rain off you, so you arrive at school dry.
quests.funFact: Umbrellas were first used for shade thousands of years ago.
